strengths: Clear, principled formulation: Guiding an unconditional 3D latent diffusion model using differentiable geometric moment losses (0th, 1st, and scale-normalized 2nd-order moments) allows training-free, test-time control of size, position, and shape.

Effective disentanglement and compositionality: The linear decomposition of moments enables modular control over individual geometric attributes, as well as arbitrary multi-component conditioning without retraining, outperforming conditional baselines trained with dropout on few-component conditioning (Table 2).

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The paper compares against multiple representative conditioning strategies (explicit concatenation, implicit distance maps, cross-attention) across both morphological distribution metrics (Fréchet Distance, Precision, Recall) and 3D pointcloud generative metrics (MMD, Coverage, 1-NNA).

Grounding in downstream biophysical simulation: Demonstrating an end-to-end pipeline from guided inpainting to tetrahedral meshing and finite-element biomechanical pressurization simulations validates the practical utility of the framework for digital twins and in silico trials.
weaknesses: Inference latency and computational complexity: Backpropagating through the 3D VAE decoder at every reverse diffusion step to compute geometric moments in voxel space incurs notable memory and computational overhead, but exact runtime, wall-clock comparisons, and memory footprints are not reported.

Sensitivity and loss scaling: The moment loss weights span several orders of magnitude (from 10^4 to 10^7, Table 5) and require manual tuning per application. In addition, handling degenerate/empty components requires heuristic noise stabilization to prevent zero-division in moment calculation.

Expressiveness of ellipsoidal moments: Second-order moments essentially constrain an equivalent bounding ellipsoid. While effective for compact chambers and bulk structures, they may provide weaker shape control for highly irregular, tortuous, or branching geometries (e.g., peripheral vasculature) without manual sub-segmentation.

Limited dataset domain: The framework is evaluated exclusively on cardiac structures from TotalSegmentator; evaluating or discussing transferability to other anatomical regimes (e.g., musculoskeletal or abdominal organs) would further substantiate the general applicability claims.

strengths: Principled and practical formulation: Formulating inference-time geometric guidance for 3D multi-label segmentation diffusion models through differentiable zeroth-, first-, and second-order moments provides an elegant, training-free mechanism for independent control of anatomical size, position, and orientation/aspect ratio.

Compositionality and flexibility: Unlike conditional diffusion models that require fixed conditioning schemes or retraining with dropouts, the proposed guidance framework operates on arbitrary subsets of anatomical structures at inference time, showing superior performance when only a few components are constrained.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The paper compares against three competitive conditional architectures (explicit concatenation with adaptive null guidance, implicit Mahalanobis distance maps with classifier-free guidance, and cross-attention tokens) across both geometric fidelity metrics and generative distribution quality metrics (morphological Fréchet distance, precision/recall, and point cloud EMD-based MMD, coverage, and 1-NNA).

End-to-end clinical and biophysical utility: The downstream demonstration using finite-element biventricular pressurization simulations convincingly illustrates how the controllable generative framework can produce digital siblings for counterfactual biomechanical analysis.

Clear writing and extensive implementation details: The paper and appendix thoroughly specify hyperparameter configurations, loss weights, meshing routines, and simulation parameters, supporting reproducibility.
weaknesses: Significant computational overhead at inference: Guiding the reverse diffusion trajectory requires running the 3D VAE decoder, computing soft binarization, extracting moments, and backpropagating gradients through both the moment loss and the 3D convolutional decoder at every denoising iteration. The paper lacks an empirical analysis of wall-clock sampling time and peak GPU memory compared to baseline conditional models.

Expressivity limited by low-order moments: Second-order moments essentially parameterize 3D ellipsoids. While the authors demonstrate that complex branched or curved structures (e.g., aorta, vena cava) can be guided globally, the method cannot enforce localized shape modifications (such as local wall thickness variations, luminal tapering, or branching angles) that are often crucial in hemodynamic simulations.

Numerical sensitivity with small or disappearing structures: Because computing centroids and scale-normalized covariances involves division by total component mass, small or degenerated segmentations can produce numerical instability or gradient explosions. The proposed mitigation (adding noise to the denominator) is empirical and may require delicate tuning depending on label volume scales.

Evaluation limited to a single anatomical domain: The evaluation is restricted to 596 cropped cardiac CT segmentations from TotalSegmentator. Demonstrating applicability on an additional anatomical domain with differing geometry (e.g., musculoskeletal or abdominal multi-organ structures) would significantly strengthen the claims of generalizability.

strengths: Elegant and training-free formulation: Using differentiable 0th, 1st, and 2nd geometric moments to guide reverse diffusion enables test-time controllable generation of 3D anatomical structures without the need to retrain conditional diffusion models.

Disentanglement and compositionality: The separation into volume, centroid, and scale-normalized covariance allows independent control of size, position, and shape, as well as flexible compositional conditioning over arbitrary subsets of anatomical labels.

Comprehensive downstream validation: The paper connects generative modeling to downstream engineering utility by demonstrating mesh extraction and finite element biomechanical simulations (pressurization of ventricles) on counterfactual edits.

Solid empirical evaluation: The method is compared against appropriate conditioning baselines (explicit vector concatenation, implicit distance maps, and cross-attention) across both morphological distribution metrics and 3D point-cloud metrics.
weaknesses: Inference latency and computational overhead: Performing full 3D VAE decoding and backpropagation through the decoder and moment extraction pipeline at every diffusion step incurs significant compute and memory overhead, but wall-clock runtime and memory consumption comparisons against feedforward conditional models are not reported.

Sensitivity to gradient stability heuristics: The approach relies on engineering heuristics (e.g., softmax temperature of 0.01, injecting artificial noise into the denominator to avoid division-by-zero on empty/near-empty components, and large disparities in loss weighting: 10^7 vs 10^5 vs 10^4), indicating potential optimization fragility.

Limited dataset diversity and scale: Experiments are restricted to a single cardiac CT cohort of 596 cases at a relatively coarse isotropic resolution of 2 mm; validating on other organ systems (e.g., brain, musculoskeletal) or higher resolutions would substantiate the generality of the method.

Generation quality trade-off at full conditioning: When all components are actively constrained, the trained implicit conditioning baseline performs comparably or slightly better on morphological Fréchet Distance and point-cloud metrics (Table 2).

strengths: Principled and elegant formulation: The paper introduces a training-free, inference-time guidance framework that uses differentiable geometric moments (zeroth-order for mass/size, first-order for centroid/position, and scale-normalized second-order for shape/orientation) to control 3D multi-class anatomical generation.

Strong disentanglement and compositionality: The proposed method allows flexible, independent control over distinct geometric features and seamlessly composes constraints over arbitrary subsets of substructures without retraining the base diffusion model, outperforming standard conditional baselines trained with dropout.

Convincing downstream utility: The practical value of the generated anatomies is nicely showcased through biophysical finite element simulations of biventricular pressurization, demonstrating meaningful changes in physiological wall mechanics.

Thorough evaluation across diverse anatomies: The method is validated on multiple distinct anatomical structures (heart, aorta, spine, and knee) and supported by extensive quantitative evaluations spanning morphological distribution metrics, point-cloud shape metrics, and topological analysis (Betti numbers).
weaknesses: Inference latency and computational cost: Guiding reverse diffusion by decoding latent representations to full voxel grids and backpropagating through both the VAE decoder and moment extraction operations at each sampling step introduces non-trivial runtime and memory overhead compared to feedforward conditional models.

Topological integrity challenges: While conditional fidelity is substantially improved, geometric gradient guidance can occasionally exacerbate topological defects (e.g., disconnected components in thin vascular structures as indicated by the Betti error analysis in Table 8), requiring post-hoc topological filtering.

Disparate loss weighting scales: The moment loss terms operate at drastically different numerical scales (weights ranging from 10^4 to 10^7), necessitating careful hyperparameter tuning to avoid numerical instabilities or dominating gradients.

strengths: Principled and practical formulation: The paper proposes an elegant, inference-time guidance framework using differentiable 0th, 1st, and 2nd order geometric moments (mass, centroid, scale-normalized covariance) to achieve disentangled and compositional control (size, position, shape) over 3D multi-organ anatomical diffusion models without requiring conditional retraining.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The authors benchmark against multiple competitive conditioning baselines (explicit scalar concatenation, implicit Gaussian distance fields, and cross-attention) across diverse metrics including conditional fidelity, morphological distribution fidelity (Precision, Recall, Fréchet Morphological Distance), pointcloud metrics (MMD, COV, 1-NNA), and topological consistency (Betti errors).

Real-world downstream validation: The paper validates the generated anatomical variations using an end-to-end biophysical simulation pipeline (biventricular pressurization finite element analysis), directly demonstrating the utility of the method for in silico trials and digital twin workflows.

Versatility across anatomical domains: The framework is shown to be flexible, supporting single-class control, multi-class unions, inpainting, and generalizing across multiple distinct anatomical datasets (whole heart, branched aorta, CT spine, and knee).
weaknesses: High computational cost at inference: The method computes the geometric loss by decoding latents to 3D voxel space (128^3 resolution) and backpropagating gradients through the 3D VAE decoder at every denoising iteration. The manuscript lacks an empirical wall-clock time and GPU memory footprint comparison against standard unconditional or conditional sampling.

Geometric expressiveness limited to ellipsoidal approximations: Because the loss relies solely on second-order moments, it inherently approximates substructures as ellipsoidal primitives. For highly non-convex, curved, or tortuous structures (such as branching vascular trees or thin walls), these moments are coarse summary statistics that cannot constrain local curvature, lumen diameter, or complex branching geometry.

Topological degradation under strong guidance: As shown in Table 8, gradient guidance can exacerbate topological defects (higher connected-component Betti errors for structures like the pulmonary artery and inferior vena cava) because the moment-matching objective does not penalize fragmentation as long as mass, centroid, and covariance targets are met.

Heuristic stabilization required: As noted in the appendix, the denominator in centroid and covariance computations causes numerical instabilities and exploding gradients when predicted organ masks are sparse or near-empty, necessitating heuristic noise injection to maintain optimization stability.

strengths: Clear, intuitive, and technically sound formulation: using differentiable geometric moments (zeroth, first, and scale-normalized second-order moments) to guide unconditional 3D latent diffusion models at inference time without requiring retraining.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation that compares the proposed guidance approach against multiple strong conditional baselines (explicit concatenation, implicit distance-map conditioning, and cross-attention), demonstrating superior compositional control and fidelity-quality trade-offs.
Convincing validation of disentangled attribute control (independent manipulation of mass, centroid, aspect ratio, and orientation) both qualitatively and quantitatively.

Demonstrated generality across multiple anatomical systems (cardiac structures, branched aorta, spinal column, and knee condyle/cartilage) as well as an end-to-end downstream application to finite element biomechanical simulations.
Thorough appendix providing extensive ablations and analyses, including dataset scaling, VAE reconstruction bounds, topological Betti error, and fine-grained moment decompositions.
weaknesses: Computational overhead and inference speed: Computing gradients through the 3D VAE decoder and moment extraction at every reverse diffusion step adds significant computational cost compared to feed-forward conditional generation, but runtime measurements and memory footprints are not explicitly reported.

Impact on topological integrity: As documented in Appendix Table 8 and Section 6, geometric guidance can exacerbate topological defects (e.g., increased Betti errors / disconnected components for vessels like the pulmonary artery and inferior vena cava), which can pose hurdles for automated meshing pipelines.

Representation limited to second-order ellipsoidal approximations: While second moments capture size, centroid, and overall orientation/aspect ratio, they cannot explicitly control finer localized geometric features such as lumen tortuosity, branching angles, or local cross-sectional wall thickness.
